questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I just wanted to mix things up and try something new. It's a great university in a beautiful country with interesting culture.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My priority was to experience being on exchange without feeling I was compromising the academic outcome of my semester.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Once I arrived the information found me naturally.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There is an intro meeting which is nice and some information emails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got housing at a WOKO dorm by applying for housing through the exchange office. It was easy and they house quite a lot of people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The public transport is very painless to use and living ~25 minutes from my campus in the city center was not a problem at all. Biking to uni is possible and many of my friends did it but be aware that some of the hills/mountains are quite steep (especially if you have to go from Altstetten or Zentrum to Hönggerberg.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a ton of fun living in a WOKO dorm with a lot of other exchange students. Some of the facilities were a bit frustrating (the kitchen mainly) and WOKO as an organisation was also a bit frustrating.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process is very flexible.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can register/deregister for courses courses until two weeks into the semester. It is very common to register for more courses than you would like to complete and then use the first two weeks attending the intro lectures to decide which courses you want to keep. After the two weeks you registration is still not very binding/demanding. While you cannot deregister anymore you can simply choose to not register for the exam. Even if you register for the exam you can still afterwards deregister from the exam (in many cases up until the day before the exam) effectively on paper making it as if you never attended the course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could correspond with our exchange coordinators via E-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register to all classes that I wanted but the main problem was balancing the timeslots and credits of the courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would generally say be careful about choosing many small (few ects) courses as some of them are more work than proclaimed. Also if you are in doubt about which course to keep after the two weeks registration window just keep e.g. both of them and decide a little further down the road. While you may be taking up one more spot on a course that you will stop attending it might save you a lot of trouble.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You learn a lot because you have to work a lot. Sometimes the work/lectures can feel a bit time inefficient and in my opinion many of the exams test memory and how much you prepared for the exam more than how much you understand the course material.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The difficulty of my course were in general roughly the same or slightly higher than back home. The workload/credit was higher.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I did Big Data, Probabilistic AI, Visual Computing and Natural Language Processing. Big data has a great professor and is not too difficult considering that it is 10 ECTS. NLP and Probabilistic AI are quite demanding in terms of math and abstraction but are both great courses in their own ways (NLP had a lot of hickups in the assignments but it was the first iteration with assignments so I suspect this will have improved a lot). Probabilistic AI was probably my favorite course as it is really hard to point to anything specific they could improve in the course. NLP is conceptually very interesting but do not expect a course that is centered around deep learning and transformers. The course mainly deals with various ways to model probability distributions over language structure and then making simplifying assumptions such that normalization constants can be calculated efficiently with abstract (semirings) dynamic programming. Visual computing is very mediocre. The professors have very impressive achievements but in my opinion the teaching was quite poor. The course has a lot of content and almost none was very thoroughly explained.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Probabilistic AI, Big Data, NLP in no particular order. I did not attend it but I think you learn a lot on the Deep Learning course but it is probably quite tough. Did not hear good thing about advanced machine learning. Introduction to machine learning has the same professor as Probabilistic AI and he is very good.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: ASVZ is very nice considering it is free.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sorts. Look at ASVZ's webpage for sport/fitness opportunities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did a hackathon and it was a great exprerience. Came for the free food and stuff but looking back I would almost have done it without the free food (almost ;) )

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is so much to do. Nature and skiing is great. Zurich is very central so you can easily take the train to Milano or Paris.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just speak with them. The swiss can seem a bit introvert.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The tidiness and order.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Consider how you want to spent your time of the exchange. (e.g. is it okay to spent a lot of time studying or would you rather have less ects and more time for travel)
2. The time spent for exchange preparation, application, etc. is worth it and once you are there you just have to attend uni and have fun.
3. Accept that something unexpected may happen. Many people fail/drop a course and often exams are held during the beginning of the next semester back.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Taking the train between Zürich and Copenhagen is really not that bad if you take the train during the day. It is cheaper and you don't have to worry about weight/number of pieces of luggage.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Almost every part was rewarding in its own way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The workload was tough but expected given I took 34 credits.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
